summary: Math.max returns the greatest of its numeric arguments.
documentation: Math.max returns the greatest of its numeric arguments. It accepts individual arguments rather than an array; spreading a small array supplies those arguments. With no arguments it returns negative infinity.
returns: The greatest number; negative infinity for no arguments.
caution: Handle empty input before returning JSON. Spreading a very large array can exceed an engine’s argument limit.
scenarios: Find the largest stock adjustment in a small import.
Display the highest daily visitor count.
Identify a peak measured temperature in a bounded sample.
title: Find a peak reading
problem: Input is an array of at most 100 finite numbers. Return its greatest value, or null when empty. Negative values are valid, so do not use zero as an empty-array substitute.
goal: Use Math.max() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Check for an empty array before spreading it into Math.max.
